subject: english
question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

The sports teacher saw __across__ the game and punished the students who were cheating in the game.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct phrase in this context is "through the game." This phrase indicates that the teacher observed the game or the activity taking place during the game. "Through" is used to indicate an ongoing action or observation.
 
• "Underneath" refers to something being physically below something else, which does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• "Beside" means next to something, which does not make sense in this context, as it refers to physical proximity rather than observation.
 
• "Beneath" also refers to being physically under something, which does not fit the intended meaning of observing the game in this case.

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The sports teacher saw through the game and punished the students who were cheating in the game."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "underneath" **– This phrase does not fit in the context of the sentence as it refers to something physically below, which is not the intended meaning here.
 
• **Option 3: "beside" **– This phrase implies physical proximity, which does not fit with the meaning of observing a game in this context.
 
• **Option 4: "beneath" **– This also refers to something being physically under something, which is not relevant in this context.
